editorial.headline: Forest Timber: Open to PMA, Conditional in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 02102 covers timber management in forests; it is 100% foreign-open nationally, while Bali attaches a local-community partnership condition.
editorial.body:
## Forest Timber, Managed at Its Source

KBLI 02102 covers timber management within forests, from planting through felling, with roundwood as the production output. Its stated scope includes timber forest products from plantation forests and natural forests in production forests. The activity may take place in natural, semi-natural, or planted forests. The defining thread is management of the timber within the forest itself, through the stages the record names. Planting and felling are the named ends of that continuum, rather than side notes to it. The scope describes timber as a forest product managed through those stages and produced as roundwood. It identifies natural forests, semi-natural forests, and plantation forests, and specifically includes timber forest products from both plantation and natural forests in production forests.

The record opens this activity to every listed business scale: micro, small, medium, and large. That breadth does not alter the classification’s subject matter. At each of those scales, the activity remains forest-based timber management with roundwood as its output, across the forest settings set out in the scope. The scale field answers who may register it; the scope field answers what is being registered. The record lists each of these scales as open to the activity; it states no exclusion among them.

Nationally, the position is open to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100% under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Put plainly, foreign investment may own 100% of this activity at the national level. Bali adds a condition rather than a closure. The Bali record marks the activity TERBATAS, but not blocked for PMA registration, and requires a partnership with local communities. The province’s permanent PMA moratorium applies to Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI; this record does not mark this activity as blocked.

The honest Bali reading is therefore exact. Forest timber management under this classification is not closed to PMA in Bali, but its 100% national opening sits alongside the stated local-community partnership condition. That condition belongs in the registration picture from the start. For founders, the classification is neither a generic timber label nor a Bali prohibition: it is a defined forest-management activity, open across the listed scales and subject in Bali to the condition the record expressly sets out.
editorial.pullQuote: In Bali, the national 100% opening sits alongside a local-community partnership condition.
